summary: Implement reusable deterministic WorldBuilder secret, route, and clue planning so generated optional areas are discoverable from semantic evidence, integrate with reusable interactable routes and canonical discovery credit, and explicitly control voxel bypass behavior.

repro.observed: WorldBuilder can author world features and the repository has separate work for reusable exploration interactables, but there is no canonical generated Secret -> Route(s) -> Clue(s) planning layer. Generated secret spaces therefore lack a reusable contract for stable identity, legal access routes, pre-solve evidence, clue diversity, deterministic validation, runtime discovery registration, or authored voxel-bypass policy. This encourages one-off secret placement and makes secret quality dependent on hand-authored scene logic.
repro.expected: WorldBuilder exposes a deterministic, constraint-driven secret planning system based on the design in Docs/worldbuilder-secret-clues-design.md. Generated secrets have stable IDs, one or more legal routes, semantically meaningful pre-solve clues, explicit importance/readability policy, and an explicit voxel-bypass policy. Route realization composes with reusable interactables rather than duplicating interaction state. Discovery/reward persistence remains owned by the canonical runtime authority. Representative generated examples in WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase demonstrate that players can infer and reach secrets from intentional evidence without wall-spamming.
steps: Open Docs/worldbuilder-secret-clues-design.md and treat its Secret -> Route(s) -> Clue(s) model and responsibility split as the primary design contract for this feature.

Open Assets/Scenes/WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase.unity and identify representative generated world features suitable for secret-planning demonstrations, including at least one architectural secret and one natural/terrain secret where practical.
Generate the same secret-bearing feature twice from identical inputs/seed and verify stable secret, route, clue, and anchor selection output.

Verify a Standard secret receives at least one meaningful pre-solve clue and a Major secret receives at least two clues across independent channels unless explicitly overridden by authored constraints.
Verify required clues are observable before the route is solved and do not depend circularly on entering or opening the secret they explain.
Verify clue planning uses semantic anchors/roles rather than direct prefab names or capture-specific coordinates.
Verify at least one route is realized through the reusable exploration-interactable system when that route kind requires an interactable, without adding a second interaction authority.
Verify a secret with multiple legitimate routes maps all routes back to one stable discovery identity.
Verify each authored route declares a voxel bypass policy and demonstrate ProtectedShell, AuthoredBreakablesOnly, or SystemicBypassAllowed behavior where applicable.
Verify protected secrets do not have an obvious unintended one-voxel bypass and authored breakable routes do not accidentally expose surrounding protected geometry.
Verify entering a generated secret registers discovery through the canonical runtime discovery authority and revisiting/reloading does not duplicate credit or rewards.

Verify the built WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase reaches a usable rendered state without runtime exceptions and the generated clues are visually readable at gameplay scale without resorting to universal glowing-secret markers.

notes:
DESIGN SOURCE
- Primary design: Docs/worldbuilder-secret-clues-design.md.
- Existing WorldBuilder/world-feature authoring conventions remain authoritative where the design document uses illustrative type names. Do not introduce parallel abstractions when an existing repository-native type can own the responsibility.
- The existing ExplorationInteractablesSecretsShowcase SceneIssue explicitly leaves procedural placement/generation rules for interactables or secrets out of scope; this issue owns that missing procedural planning layer.

CORE MODEL
Implement the semantic relationship Secret -> Route(s) -> Clue(s).
- Secret: stable hidden region/optional destination and discovery identity.
- Route: a legal access path or mechanism.
- Clue: intentional pre-solve evidence that lets the player infer the secret or route.
- Discovery: runtime first-credit event owned outside WorldBuilder.
- Bypass policy: explicit rule describing how voxel modification/systemic traversal may circumvent the authored route.

RESPONSIBILITY BOUNDARIES
- WorldBuilder planner owns deterministic route/clue selection, semantic attachment, constraints, and validation.
- Reusable interactable runtime owns mechanism behavior/state/replication for doors, trapdoors, pressure plates, pushables, barriers, lifts, or other accepted mechanisms.
- Clue realization owns presentation only and must not become another interaction/discovery state machine.
- Canonical runtime discovery authority owns first-discovery detection, persistence, party credit, reward grants, reload behavior, and duplicate prevention.
- Physical loot is independent from discovery credit; a secret does not require a chest.

PLANNING CONTRACT
Introduce repository-appropriate equivalents of:
- stable SecretId / SecretRouteId / SecretClueId;
- secret importance/readability classification;
- route kind;
- clue channel;
- semantic clue-anchor role/metadata;
- route bypass policy;
- immutable or otherwise stable generated secret/route/clue plan output.
Names in the design doc are illustrative. Prefer existing value-object and descriptor conventions.

SEMANTIC CLUE AUTHORING
World-feature templates/nodes should expose candidate semantic clue anchors rather than hard-coding prefab names. Initial roles should cover concepts such as approach evidence, exterior evidence, route-adjacent evidence, sightline hint, acoustic hint, traversal hint, and narrative hint where supported. Candidate metadata must be sufficient to determine supported clue channels, observable side/region, bounds/facing, pre-solve reachability, useful distance, hidden-volume relation, and compatibility constraints.

DETERMINISTIC PLANNING
At minimum:
1. Select/plan hidden destination.
2. Select legal route candidates.
3. Derive clue requirements from importance/difficulty/route.
4. Gather compatible pre-solve clue anchors.
5. Score candidates for observability, relevance, diversity, distance, duplication/overexposure, and thematic fit.
6. Select deterministically from seed plus stable tie-breaking.
7. Validate clue count/diversity/observability/dependency topology.
8. Emit stable plan data for realization/runtime registration.
Do not silently generate an unsolvable secret when required clue topology cannot be satisfied; fail validation or select a deterministic documented fallback.

DEFAULT READABILITY POLICY
- Minor: 0-1 subtle clue.
- Standard: at least 1 meaningful clue.
- Major: at least 2 clues across independent channels.
- Main-path/progression-critical hidden content must use stronger discoverability constraints and should not inherit weak optional-secret readability by accident.
- Avoid a universal glowing crack/outline language that collapses exploration into marker-following.

VOXEL BYPASS POLICY
Support explicit authored policy equivalent to:
- ProtectedShell: preserve the intended access puzzle/route against arbitrary voxel bypass.
- AuthoredBreakablesOnly: explicitly designated destructible barrier is legal while surrounding shell remains constrained.
- SystemicBypassAllowed: player-created traversal/destruction may legitimately bypass the authored route and still discover the same secret.
Validate that protected shells do not contain trivial accidental holes/bypasses and that authored breakables do not leak destructibility into surrounding geometry.

DISCOVERY AND REWARD INTEGRATION
- WorldBuilder emits stable metadata sufficient for canonical runtime registration.
- Do not create showcase-local or WorldBuilder-owned save state.
- Revisit/reload and repeated mechanism toggles must not duplicate discovery credit or rewards.
- Multiple legal routes to one secret must credit one SecretId.
- Multiplayer discovery should remain authoritative/idempotent under the canonical discovery system.
- Discovery XP should normally be party/shared when the progression system supports it.
- Standard/Major optional content should be capable of referencing evergreen rewards whose value does not strongly depend on player level, but defining the final progression currency/system is not owned here.

REPRESENTATIVE CONTENT
Demonstrate at least three representative secret patterns across generated content where the underlying world-feature systems support them:
- Architectural hidden volume such as attic/room with spatial or navigation evidence and an interactable route.
- Hidden chamber/ruin with mechanical/environmental evidence and a pushable/breakable/activation route.
- Natural terrain/cave secret with traversal/environmental clues and no required interactable.
If an existing generated feature cannot reasonably support one pattern without unrelated expansion, document the limitation and use another representative generated feature rather than adding capture-specific geometry.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Docs/worldbuilder-secret-clues-design.md is present on master and implementation follows its responsibility boundaries or documents a repository-native improvement.
- Stable secret/route/clue identity and plan metadata exist.
- Same inputs and seed produce the same secret/route/clue plan.
- Secret importance/readability drives clue requirements.
- Standard and Major clue-count/channel rules are behaviorally tested.
- Required clues are provably pre-solve observable and circular clue dependencies fail validation.
- Semantic clue anchors are reusable across feature types and are not prefab-name or capture-coordinate contracts.
- At least one interactable-backed route composes through the accepted reusable interactable abstractions, with no duplicate interaction state machine.
- At least one natural traversal route demonstrates that secrets do not require interactables.
- Multiple routes to one secret resolve to one discovery identity.
- Explicit voxel bypass policy is represented and behaviorally tested, including accidental protected-shell bypass prevention.
- Canonical discovery integration is idempotent across revisit/reload and does not live in WorldBuilder/showcase-local persistence.
- Representative generated examples are visible and understandable in WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase at gameplay scale.
- Focused EditMode/PlayMode regressions cover determinism, clue policy, observability, dependency validation, route identity, and bypass policy.
- Built-application SceneIssue validation runs the exact WorldbuildingGalleryShowcase scene and proves it reaches a usable rendered state without runtime exceptions.
- Visual review confirms clues communicate intentional evidence through geometry/material/environmental language and do not degrade into placeholder signs or universal glowing markers.

DEPENDENCY / INTEGRATION RULE
The implementation may depend on reusable interactable/discovery APIs delivered by SceneIssues/open/20260830-014314-000-ExplorationInteractablesSecretsShowcase. Do not duplicate missing APIs simply to unblock this feature. Planner/model/validation work that is independent may proceed, but integration must bind to the canonical reusable systems once available.

OUT OF SCOPE
- A full quest system.
- Final definition of the global XP/mastery/evergreen progression economy.
- A visual puzzle graph editor.
- Rebuilding the reusable interactable inventory owned by the existing interactables SceneIssue.
- WorldBuilder-owned save-game persistence.
- Mandatory loot chests for secrets.
- Capture-specific coordinates or one-off secret scripts.
- Implementing all future clue presentation channels such as final narrative/audio systems if those systems do not yet exist; the semantic contracts should permit them without blocking the initial feature.
